entities.name: Benzyl ether debenzylation
observations: Reactant decodes to ClC1=CC=C(C2=CSC(COCC3=CC=CC=C3)=N2)C=C1; product is OCC1=NC(C2=CC=C(Cl)C=C2)=CS1.
The transformation cleaves the O–CH2Ph bond of a benzyl ether to give the corresponding hydroxymethyl group; the heterocycle and aryl chloride are retained.
Closest/essentially exact ORD record uses BBr3 in dichloromethane, followed by bicarbonate-containing aqueous/basic workup.

entities.name: Boron tribromide
observations: Most likely active deprotection reagent for cleavage of the benzyl ether in this reaction; used in dichloromethane.

entities.name: BBr3 in dichloromethane
observations: Likely reaction medium for Lewis-acid-mediated ether cleavage; aqueous/basic bicarbonate workup follows.

entities.name: Sodium bicarbonate
observations: Likely aqueous/basic quench or workup component after BBr3-mediated deprotection; not the bond-forming reagent.
